content: Sodium acetate is a sodium-based compound that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of hyponatremia. It is commonly used as an additive to large-volume intravenous fluids to either prevent or correct low sodium levels in patients who are unable to take sodium orally. It is also utilized in the preparation of specific intravenous fluid formulations when standard electrolyte or nutrient solutions are insufficient to meet the patient’s needs. The administration of Sodium Acetate Injection, USP 40 mEq, is strictly intravenous and must always be diluted in a larger volume of fluid before use. The dosage and rate of administration are tailored to the individual patient’s needs, and serum sodium levels should be closely monitored to guide therapy. Using aseptic techniques, the contents of one or more vials can be added to other intravenous fluids to achieve the desired sodium concentration, with an equivalent amount of acetate ions provided. Sodium acetate is contraindicated in patients with hypernatremia (elevated sodium levels) or fluid retention. It must be used with caution in patients with conditions such as congestive heart failure, severe renal insufficiency, or other states associated with sodium retention and edema. In patients with impaired renal function, sodium retention may occur. Additionally, solutions containing acetate ions should be used cautiously in patients with metabolic or respiratory alkalosis, as well as in those with severe hepatic insufficiency, where acetate metabolism may be impaired. The intravenous administration of sodium acetate, even after proper dilution, carries risks such as fluid overload, dilution of other serum electrolytes, overhydration, congestive states, or pulmonary edema. Excessive administration of potassium-free solutions may lead to significant hypokalemia. Furthermore, this product contains aluminum, which can accumulate to toxic levels, particularly in patients with impaired kidney function or in premature neonates. Toxic levels of aluminum are associated with central nervous system and bone toxicity. Sodium acetate should not be administered unless the solution is clear and the seal is intact. Any unused portion should be discarded. Sodium replacement therapy should be guided primarily by serum sodium levels. Special caution is required when administering sodium-containing solutions to patients with severe renal impairment, cirrhosis, cardiac failure, or other conditions associated with sodium retention or edema. Patients receiving corticosteroids or corticotropin should also be monitored closely. Excessive administration of acetate ions can result in metabolic alkalosis. Adverse reactions to sodium acetate include sodium overload, which may occur if excessive amounts of sodium-containing solutions are infused intravenously. Sodium Acetate Injection, USP 40 mEq (2 mEq/mL), is a sterile, nonpyrogenic solution of sodium acetate in water for injection. It is intended for intravenous use as an electrolyte replenisher after appropriate dilution. Each 20 mL vial contains 3.28 g of sodium acetate (anhydrous), providing 40 mEq of sodium and acetate ions. The solution does not contain any bacteriostatic or antimicrobial agents. The pH of the solution is adjusted to 6.5 (range: 6.0 to 7.0) using acetic acid. The solution is an alternative to sodium chloride for providing sodium ions in large-volume infusion fluids. Sodium acetate is classified as Pregnancy Category C by the FDA, meaning that animal reproduction studies have not been conducted, and it is not known whether sodium acetate can cause fetal harm or affect reproductive capacity. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly necessary. There is no specific guidance on its use during labor and delivery, in nursing mothers, or in patients with hepatic or renal impairment. In elderly patients, dose selection should be cautious, starting at the lower end of the dosing range, due to the increased likelihood of decreased hepatic, renal, or cardiac function and the presence of other medical conditions or concurrent drug therapies. Sodium acetate is supplied in 20 mL single-dose plastic vials, partially filled to allow for complete vacuum withdrawal of the contents. The product should be stored at controlled room temperature, between 20° and 25°C (68° to 77°F).
